discrepancies.claim: dead_ends item 1: 'NEITHER modern channel has any archived history for any product in this gate ... The single exception in this gate is productId 166, one capture at timestamp 20210710091114'; and the matching states entry 'the gate's request to date when each channel said what is answerable only for the server-rendered spec pages and the CFTC filings, not for either modern channel'.
discrepancies.finding: FALSE as written. The researcher's CDX sweep covered only productIds 7968, 7969, 8027, 7948, 7949, 8026 and 166. productId 133 - the ES underlying record the ruling itself leans on as one of its seven venue-labelled statements - was never swept. It has 23 archived captures (11 distinct digests) of /CmeWS/mvc/ContractSpecs/List/productId/133, running 2021-07-03 through 2026-04-05. Nine were replayed and read this pass; every one carries the venue-labelled 'CME Globex: ... BTIC: Sunday - Friday 6:00 p.m. - 4:00 p.m. ET' line. (8314, 170, 7945, 7596, 7946, 7947, 8315 were also swept independently and are genuinely empty.)
discrepancies.why_it_matters: AGENTS.md legislates this exact failure: "'Unsourced' means 'not worked up', never 'no source exists'" - do not write that nothing survives unless the channel has actually been searched. Under LAW-FOLLOW-UPS-ARE-ISSUES a channel recorded as exhausted is a tracked claim the next reader will believe, and this one would steer a future session away from a channel holding eleven distinct dated states of the very line the gate adjudicates. The error cuts IN FAVOUR of the ruling, not against it - but it is still a false statement about the evidence base.
discrepancies.correct_statement: The BTIC *product* records (7968, 7969, 8027, 7949, 7970) and the session-event service have no archived history and cannot be ordered in time. The *underlying* records the ruling relies on do: productId 133 is archived 2021-07-03 -> 2026-04-05 (23 captures, 11 distinct digests) and productId 166 once at 2021-07-10. The modern channel therefore CAN be dated for the 2021-2026 era, and when dated it says 16:00 ET throughout.

discrepancies.severity: minor - unnoticed counter-datum to the *explanation*, not to the ruling
discrepancies.claim: Conclusion item 1: every 17:00 ET reading is 'the ClearPort BTIC window with its label dropped'; CME publishes 'a CME ClearPort ("CPC") BTIC window of 18:00-17:00 ET'.
discrepancies.finding: True at launch (the 2015 NPS prints CPC at 18:00-17:00 ET) and true of 7969's ClearPort row today. But the researcher's own cs-133-live.txt - quoted in the same result for its Globex line - carries a ClearPort row that reads 'BTIC: Sunday - Friday 6:00 p.m. - 4:00 p.m. ET. BTICs for the following trading day can be submitted after 7:00 p.m. ET', i.e. CME's current ES record puts the CLEARPORT BTIC line at 16:00 ET too, and has since at least the 2022-09-08 archived capture. The 17:00 figure on 7969 and 8027 is the GENERIC ClearPort envelope, not a BTIC-specific ClearPort window. The ruling is unaffected (it concerns the Globex window) but the 'two BTIC windows' framing should be stated as 'the generic ClearPort envelope' rather than 'the ClearPort BTIC window'.

checks_that_found_nothing_wrong: Every verbatim quote in the result was matched against the saved bytes. No silently stitched line changes a meaning; no wrong time; no wrong zone label. The 2018/2019 quote is a composite of two captures but both carry the quoted lines identically, and the 2021 notice quote is three consecutive paragraphs of one section.

Issue date vs effective date vs capture date are kept distinct throughout, and capture_ts is separated from artifact_date in every states entry. The one place a capture is used to date a state (the 2015-11-15 page) is handled correctly - note the page's own wording there is future tense ('For the BTIC, trading hours WILL BE'), because 08:30 UTC on 2015-11-15 is ~14 hours before the launch session opened; the identical text recurs post-launch on 2016-02-01 and in the present tense from 2017, so nothing rests on the future-tense capture alone.

Conditional vs unconditional is graded correctly in every case: NPS footer conditional -> cannot key the day; SER-8788 conditional twice -> cannot key the 2021 day; 15-438/15-437 and 18-070 unconditional -> can.

LAW-SESSION-NOT-EXPIRY: the Termination-of-Trading rows on the 2018/2019 pages and on productIds 166/133 are identified as expiry and not used. The 3:45 p.m. BTIC price determination in 15-438 is identified as a pricing procedure. The 25-546 RTH window is identified as a quoting obligation. All three calls are correct.

LAW-NO-FABRICATED-DATES: no date is asserted without an unconditional day-level primary. No revision row is invented for 2021. The key's start is keyed to trade date 2015-11-16 with a Sunday 2015-11-15 opening day, which is also the right side of the 'day-level revision rows are keyed to the local opening day' rule for a wrapping session.

Carry-back: declining to carry the grid below 2015-11-16 and encoding a pre-launch closure is exactly what the January-2010-floor bullet prescribes for a launch-dated family ('which for a launch-dated venue is its pre-launch closure').

Sourced intersection: serving 16:00 ET against the isolated 17:00 ET RSV cell, and recording the conflict beside the table rather than declaring the cell wrong, matches the 'Prefer the sourced intersection to omission' convention and its ECBTC worked example.

Maintenance vs Closed: the 15:00->17:00 CT inter-trade-date gap is 2h <= 4h within one ISO week -> Maintenance, correct; Friday 15:00 -> Sunday is Closed, correct. The service's tradingDate fields confirm the gap is inter-trade-date, not same-trade-date.

Cross-zone (U-8): September (CDT) vs December (CST) already spans the US DST change and both read 15:00 CT; I added a 2026-10-25 week and it also reads 15:00 CT. America/Chicago anchoring is right and U-8 genuinely does not reach this shape.

Product-neutral family selection: treating IPT/RVT/EMT and the 18-070 sector roots as caller catalog data joining an already-running family clock matches 'Adding or revising a product-family key' item 2. The unlocated IPT/RVT listing certifications are correctly not a blocker.
LAW-PUBLIC-SOURCES: every cited artifact is publicly reachable without authentication. No paywalled or member-portal material is relied on.

The channel caveat (r.jina.ai in front of cmegroup.com because of the IP-level block) is disclosed, and the four CFTC filings plus the archive replays - which carry the whole ruling - are caveat-free. I re-confirmed the block today.
residual_caveats_if_the_result_is_used: Re-state dead_ends item 1 per D1 before it reaches any ledger or handoff row; as written it would retire a channel that holds eleven distinct dated states of the adjudicated line.

The Sunday 16:00 / Mon-Thu 16:45 CT Pre-Open onsets still rest on the live session service alone, with no archived history and no CME prose. They are order-entry-class, correctly labelled as such, and they are carried back to 2015-11-16 under the carry-back convention with no cutover asserted - which is permissible, but the row should say so.

The sector BTIC roots from 18-070 (XYT..BIT) were never probed in the session service; they rest on the filing's prose alone. That is sufficient, but it is a one-channel sourcing for those eleven roots.
U-4 (regular vs extended) genuinely remains open for this shape; the key cannot be written without it (D8).
